item.title: Neural Networks for Physicists: From One Neuron to Attention
item.author: yzj5306@psu.edu (Yiyang Jiang)
item.description:
Presenter Mu-Yang Chen (Prof. Chao-Xing Liu’s group, Penn State)
Date August 3, 2026 · 4:30–6:00 PM
Location Davey 339
Topic Neural networks for physicists — from one neuron to attention

A three-part pedagogical tour: what a neural network actually is and how it is trained, what attention adds once the data are sequences, and how both are being used right now in many-body physics — neural-network wavefunction ansätze optimised by variational Monte Carlo, and reduced density matrices learned without the wavefunction at all. The organising claim: a network is a very flexible fitting function, and the physics lives entirely in the details of how much of it you build in by hand.
